reason: The fixed normalized geometric and shifted-mixture masses, finite first/second moments, unit mean difference quotients, variance limit and uniform zero-direction CDF convergence are correct. Separate support equalities, base variance, shifted-CDF/decomposition identities, exact sup-norm identity, the explicit 1/n bound and an abstract negation of Hadamard differentiability are not asserted. The retained sequence still contradicts the zero-direction requirement of a Hadamard derivative; n>=2 prevents zero denominators and invalid mixing weights.

The empirical-measure integral is the sample mean for every positive sample size, and the iid L2 positive-variance CLT uses Gaussian variance, not standard deviation. The second conjunct supplies exactly the finite-moment zero-direction witness required by part (ii) of the canonical formal content. L2 is equivalent here to the finite-mean/finite-variance standing assumptions, so no substantive extra moment assumption is hidden.

The fixed independent gap-uniform joint probability law, its density, boundedness, mean zero outside positive support, zero CEF and C1 bump CEFs with every derivative a at the mean implement the entire counterexample. The explicit negated contract is stronger in its quantified scope than the printed setting, but the additional fixed jointly continuous bounded witness itself meets the printed setting and refutes version-independent PDA well-definedness. Integrability and actual derivative existence are protected.

Equality on the open positive-density region is placed after the premise that one specified coordinate derivative already exists at the mean. The canonical formal content first asserts equality of all continuous representatives without that premise. Global measurable integrable CEFs replace representatives defined only on U. The retained derivative-transfer implication is true and nonvacuous.

The exact iid Uniform[0,1] x N(0,1) model, three-quarter-power degree, rate limits and lower liminf local integrated-square error bound along n=t^4 match the main counterexample. An everywhere least-squares fit is supplied rather than a measurable selection being constructed, and the square-root-degree endpoint probability bound is absent. Polynomial-square integrals on compact intervals are finite; the real liminf is of probabilities bounded in [0,1].

Stable-Gram population-L2 consistency and its envelope and uniform cubic-rate sufficient conditions are retained. The sharp row-envelope and finite deviation bounds are exported only for Uniform[0,1], whereas the canonical claim gives these for arbitrary compact intervals. A supplied a.e. row envelope replaces an asserted supremum; a fit is supplied rather than selected. Compact a.s. support rather than exact interval support is a valid generalization of the consistency clause. Positive dimensions make the Gram supremum finite and nonempty.

The four-atom and changed-marginal experiments, unique clipped Bernoulli MLE, exact variance and probability bounds, convergence to the marginal success probability, failure at each conditional target and unique averaged-KL optimum are retained. The displayed KL derivative formulas and exact positive averaged-KL gap are not asserted. All KL arguments are bounded strictly away from zero and one; conditional means are used only when their conditioning probabilities are positive.

The KL identity and separated approximate-MLE argument, compactness-to-separation and identified true-model conclusion are retained. The finite uniform real error envelope is required for every n including n=0, where sampleLogLikelihood is zero; consequently |M(t)|<=Delta(0,omega) uniformly in t. Positive-sample uniform convergence in probability alone does not impose this extra bound. Joint entropy/cross-entropy integrability and density domination protect the real KL identity; the consistency clause does not assume finite entropy. The added sample-zero bound is satisfiable in nondegenerate compact Bernoulli models and does not itself assume estimator consistency.

The likelihood on the exact sample (1,2,3) is unbounded along the specified positive normal-scale collapse path, and has no admissible maximizer. Componentwise lower bounds, C/scale inequality, specified C/(|B|+1) scale and the general positive-sample bound are not asserted in this theorem. General positive-sample unboundedness appears in T10. Positive scales make every admissible finite-sample density finite.

Both parts of the canonical formal content are present: unbounded likelihood and no maximizer for every nonempty all-positive sample, and compactness, continuity and attainment on every nonempty stated restriction with positive lower scale/rate bounds. The natural n=0 case added to the compact clause is harmless. Real B,S,b are automatically finite, and nonemptiness enforces compatibility of their bounds.

The two distinct correct full parameters induce identical normalized iid finite experiments; the exact two-target estimation bound, impossibility for every estimator and existence of an attained MLE selection failing at one truth are present. Compactness, continuity and likelihood attainment are explicit. The standalone likelihood upper bound of one and binomial sample-mass rewriting are absent. The zero component is the intended nonidentification mechanism, not an empty probability experiment.

Zero-weight nonidentification, compact identified likelihood consistency, a regular normal limit and the information covariance bound are retained. Consistency and Hessian envelopes are finite and uniform at every n including zero, which bounds both the population objective and local expected Hessian; the canonical asymptotic assumptions concern positive samples. QMD and local squared-remainder integrability are premises of the entire normality/efficiency clause, whereas the canonical claim adds QMD only for the information bound. These are genuine, jointly satisfiable restrictions, not a circular assumption of MLE consistency or normality. The regularity predicate for competing estimators agrees with the canonical local-alternative definition.

The specified nondegenerate iid hot-deck law, exact unbiasedness, scaled sampling-variance and bootstrap-expectation limits, positive variance gap, variance inconsistency, uniform second-moment bound and occupancy-constant inequalities are retained. Per-sample L2 premises are added for both the statistic and bootstrap variance. Explicit MAR/MCAR, overlap and continuous-score predicates, root-n tightness, an explicit uniform-integrability predicate and standard-error inconsistency are absent. This formalizes the precise mathematical counterexample, not a literal logical negation of the hedged assurance or a check of the reported empirical numbers.

The explicit hot-deck variance failure and fixed-score/response weighted-sign representation, conditional mean and conditional-variance identity are retained; L2 premises are added for the statistic and bootstrap variance. Separate design-admissibility, root-n tightness and interval/standard-error calibration conclusions are not asserted. Integrating independent fair signs at every fixed score/response vector correctly realizes the stated conditional variance, including the all-nonrespondent fallback.

The true-score version of the fixed matching design has the asserted unbiasedness, variance limits and bootstrap-variance failure, and the clipped additive intercept is consistent. Per-sample L2 premises are added. The canonical estimated-score statistic failure and equality of sample/resample matches, design-admissibility assertions, root-n tightness, explicit gap decomposition and standard-error conclusion are not part of this theorem. Intercept consistency alone would not prove the estimated-score failure; that additional assertion is actually in T16.

Estimated additive scores preserve every deterministic nearest-donor choice and hence every sample and resample matching statistic; the estimated-score bootstrap failure, intercept consistency and fixed-score/treatment weighted-sign mean/variance identities are present. Per-sample L2 premises are added. Separate ignorability/overlap/continuous-score predicates, root-n tightness, bootstrap-standard-error and confidence-interval conclusions, and the other procedural remarks are not asserted. Translation preserves the entire nearest-donor predicate, including ties, so classical choice is consistent here.

The twelve-atom conditional-independence and potential-outcome-independence witness, positivity, conditional placebo variance, unique risk fits, exact risks, scaled almost-sure F/Wald limits and rejection probabilities are present. The finite 240-observation equalities use 240 times population risks, not actual sample OLS residuals or asserted counts. The separate list of moments and pre-treatment assertion are absent. Exact rational recalculation confirms the full-risk, HC0, F and Wald constants. Singular-design and zero-denominator conventions only affect samples before eventual a.s. nonsingularity and positive residual limits.

The canonical population CEF-preservation and unique zero-placebo-coefficient conclusion under conditional independence, linear treatment CEF, second moments and full rank is present, together with the fixed counterexample when the linear CEF is dropped. The corrected passage also discusses asymptotic robust covariance and joint-test calibration; these conclusions are not formalized here. None of the population hypotheses assumes the resulting placebo coefficients are zero.

The canonical joint cell masses are represented exactly by overlapT(k)=3^(-(k+1)) and overlapC(k)=2^(-(k+2)), reindexing the positive integer covariate as k+1. Normalization, strictly positive cells and interior propensities, and failure of any uniform positivity margin are asserted. Positive cells in both arms give the same complete discrete support; there is no null-cell convention. The explicit propensity formula, 4/(k+6) rate and ceiling-selected violating covariate are not asserted, and support is not a separate predicate.
